The excitation energies of the 2+1st and 4+1st collective states in germanium isotopes (126Zn ≤ A ≤ 138Ge) have been measured using gamma-ray spectroscopy. These measurements involved the isotopes 126Zn ≤ A ≤ 138Ge created via the 112Sn(34S,xn) reaction. The resulting gamma rays were detected using the AGATA ball, which consists of 144 highly-segmented, high-purity germanium (HPGe) telescopes. This setup achieved superior energy resolution and a large acceptance angle, enabling the measurement of excitation energies for numerous germanium isotopes. The observed energy ratios E(4+)/E(2+) across the isotopic chain reveal a significant quadrupole deformation for 128Ge and 130Ge, whereas 126Zn ≤ A ≤ 138Ge display soft collective behavior. The newly acquired high-precision data for E(2+) and E(4+) in 126Zn ≤ A ≤ 138Ge have been utilized to constrain the parameters of the finite-range droplet model (FRDM) and the interacting boson model (IBM).

This study introduces a new method for accurately determining the masses of short-lived isotopes by employing the reduced magnetic rigidity ($B\rho$) defined by the first Bohr radius in Penning trap experiments. Utilizing this technique, researchers conducted precise mass ratio measurements between $^{132}$Sn and $^{116}$In against $^{130}$Te, achieving relative uncertainties as low as $10^{-11}$. These results represent a tenfold improvement in precision compared to previous state-of-the-art methods and are sufficient to resolve complex nuclear structure features, such as shape coexistence, via ab initio theoretical modeling. Furthermore, the high accuracy achieved enables direct comparisons between experimental mass data and supercomputer simulations of nuclear many-body systems. The success of this approach relies on achieving ultra-stable magnetic field conditions and leveraging the exceptional mass measurement capabilities of modern laser spectroscopy.

This piece serves as accessible introductory material for flow equation methods in lattice field theory, focusing on fully non-perturbative and speed-fast approximate integration of flow equations both temporally and spatially. These flow equations evolve the lattice action and its associated fields through an auxiliary parameter, effectively filtering out high momenta to introduce purely low-momentum interactions in standard form. Consequently, the flowing action retains the structural identity of the original lattice action but features modified, standard continuous interactions. This approach has been expanded beyond standard lattice gauge theory to encompass fermionic systems.

This paper addresses the challenge of identifying structured text within images, a task critical for recognizing code snippets, mathematical formulas, and other organized data. We investigate various strategies for incorporating textual prior knowledge into the recognition process and present the findings. We define a new benchmark, CodeBench, consisting of image-based code samples to assess codereognition systems. By biasing traditional text recognition models toward code using a sequential encoder trained on CodeBench, we achieve a 20% relative reduction in Word Error Rate (WER) compared to a baseline. We release CodeBench as an open resource to encourage further research and development in the field of structured text recognition.

This letter details a search for the exclusive production of single top quarks in proton-lead collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.02$ TeV utilizing data from the LHC, amounting to $130 \mu$b$^{-1}$ of integrated luminosity. The analysis focuses on the leptonic decay channel of the nucleon-induced charged-current single top quark ($l = e$ or $\mu$). The study employs an optimized selection strategy to enhance the signal-to-background ratio, while the remaining significance is evaluated through comparisons with Standard Model predictions.

Current state-of-the-art cross-domain Text-to-SQL models struggle with generalizing to unseen databases and natural language queries, primarily due to a lack of sufficient context and domain-specific knowledge. To address this, we introduce an end-to-end framework featuring an auxiliary task designed to enhance text-based question understanding. By leveraging the patterns of similar questions within the training data, this approach helps the model generate more accurate SQL queries. We evaluate our methodology on two widely used benchmarks, Solar and Spider, demonstrating that our system outperforms existing cross-domain Text-to-SQL approaches.

The LOFAR Two-metre Sky Survey (FIRST) represents the most extensive and sensitive radio survey to date, yet it remains unsuitable for high-precision power spectrum analyses of the total intensity image due to significant foreground contamination and incomplete calibration. Consequently, we investigate the galaxy power spectrum and bias by cross-correlating our sample with the Deep Lens Imaging survey. We identify residual foreground contamination within FIRST data, which diminishes when the flux limit is increased. Furthermore, we observe that the galaxy-slice power spectrum exhibits a dependence on source brightness, a result that aligns with findings from other surveys. Finally, we derive the galaxy bias parameter through the comparison of galaxy autocorrelation spectra with the reference data.

The high-dimensional rank lasso (HDR LASSO) addresses feature selection by optimizing a composite objective that integrates L1-norm regularization with a nonconvex, piecewise constant penalty dependent on the magnitude of each coefficient. Although recent studies have established the optimality of the solution within a neighborhood of zero, existing numerical approaches rely on heuristic strategies. This paper introduces an adaptive sieving algorithm that achieves quadratic convergence and demonstrates numerical superiority over current benchmarks, particularly in coefficient selection accuracy.

The study establishes new lower bounds on the rate of entropy production during the rapid and simultaneously gentle transport of arbitrary quantum systems. These bounds are fully determined by the system's initial state and the corresponding time-derivative squared of a Hamiltonian generating the evolution, with the resulting entropy change proven to be lower-semester-consistent. Furthermore, this entropic lower limit can be efficiently approximated through the application of second-order Zeno expansions of a type. Experimental verification of these findings was conducted on a trapped ion setup, and the results indicate that these entropy production limits hold universal applicability across diverse physical systems.

Although AI systems are increasingly recognized as essential tools for addressing climate change and environmental challenges, their own ecological footprint remains largely unexamined. This study introduces a comprehensive framework to assess the environmental performance of AI, covering the entire lifecycle from data sourcing and model creation to deployment and societal impact. Empirical evaluations of various machine learning models and their applications in environmental management provide data-driven insights, highlighting the substantial energy consumption inherent in AI. Consequently, the research underscores the critical need for integrating eco-efficiency into AI governance, offering guidance on establishing responsible standards that ensure environmental integrity.

Prescriptive procedure monitoring aims to identify opportunities for enhancing system performance and support decision-making by suggesting concrete actions. While current research predominantly addresses procedural optimization through decision theory, this paper investigates the feasibility of implementing action recommendations grounded in reinforcement learning (RL). We examine this prescriptive monitoring concept through the lens of information engineering, and beyond merely contrasting decision theory and RL approaches, we outline a broad framework for designing recommendation systems within procedural monitoring. Additionally, we demonstrate the application of this system using a simplified railway scheduling model, where the proposed prescriptive monitoring method shows superior performance over traditional free-running systems and purely diagnostic free-running approaches.

This study develops an adaptive finite element scheme based on rigorous a posteriori error estimates for a generalized non-linear Boussinesq model. The approach simultaneously addresses material heating and stress analysis, with error estimates incorporating multiple indicators that guide the efficient achievement of conflicting objectives. Specifically, the primary aim is precise thermal material heating, while a secondary focus minimizes residual mechanical stresses. By integrating separate error estimates for each goal, users can achieve an optimal balance between them. Numerical experiments validate the proposed methodology.

We demonstrate a kernelization method for a broad category of stacking problems defined on directed acyclic graphs (DAGs). This problem involves assigning values to DAG nodes such that every edge adheres to a specified constraint, with the objective of minimizing the total values assigned. We examine various stacking problems that utilize linear constraints combined with specific semiring properties, including standard integer and cost-weighted real numbers, extended reals, and the tropical rational function field. Our findings establish an algorithm capable of producing a kernel of exponential size relative to a constant derived based on the graph's minimum vertex degree. This algorithm compresses any solution exceeding this exponential threshold, reducing it to one of at most this size without loss of optimality.

In an era characterized by the rapid expansion of social media, individuals are frequently exposed to vast quantities of information, which often leads to uncertainty about the veracity of news and the credibility of sources. This study introduces a novel framework that integrates the propagation of information with the evolution of individual opinions and trust. The proposed model, which relies on minimal assumptions, demonstrates that even when people process only a small fraction of available data, they inevitably experience a decline in confidence. Furthermore, we analyze how the balance of opinions and social network structures influence credibility assessment. Our findings reveal a significant interaction between structural balance and opinion dynamics: individuals tend to adopt views similar to their neighbors while simultaneously adjusting their trust levels accordingly. Crucially, we observe that confidence levels are more sensitive to shifts in opinion dynamics than to changes within the network structure itself.

We examine black hole-like objects featuring a hairy surface, a phenomenon that can result from a scalar field acquiring a non-trivial minimum in its potential. Our analysis reveals that within this interior, the scalar field's energy density decreases monotonically, whereas the anisotropic stresses exhibit a distinct minimum before rising sharply to diverge at the boundary. The object's total mass scales with the power of the scalar field's energy density integrated across the interior volume. Furthermore, surface gravity is found to be zero, aligning with the object's non-stellar nature, while the entropy is proportional to that of a standard black hole but remains contingent on the boundary radius of the hairy region.

Although delays in gene transcription are recognized for their functional importance, the specific mechanisms driving these lags remain elusive. We introduce a computational framework that captures the full spectrum of timing variations—from instantaneous to significant delays—in both immediate and delayed promoter systems. By applying this model to genomic data from *E. coli*, we identified distinct temporal patterns in real biological processes that align with either physically immediate or highly delayed promoter mechanisms. Furthermore, we developed an algorithm to infer the kinetic parameters governing gene expression based on single-molecule RNA counts over time. When tested against simulated datasets, this inference method demonstrated robust accuracy. Finally, we observed that biologically derived delay distributions differ markedly from those produced by purely temporal processes, displaying instead distinct two-step characteristics indicative of dual promotion mechanisms involving rapid and slow initiation.

The quadrupole-monopole force interaction significantly influences low-lying nuclear spectra and has been extensively examined within Interacting Boson Model (IBM) frameworks. This study investigates its specific impact on the zero-spin-to-zero-one energy spacing in $^{64}$Ni, a metric crucial for identifying shape coexistence. Our findings indicate that the quadrupole-monopole force markedly accelerates the transition from a purely spherical configuration in the $IBM-1$ to a coexistence of spherical and degenerate $N=4$ $\otimes$ $N=4$ multiplets at low excitations in $IBM-4$ within the $N=4$ $\otimes$ $N=4$ limit. Notably, this interaction enhances the energy difference between the 0$^+$_2 and 2$^+$_1 states in $IBM-4$ beyond the shift observed in $IBM-1$, thereby serving as a primary driver of the coexistence of distinct shapes at zero excitation energy.

This study examines several proposed dualities involving chiral fermions and U(1) gauge symmetries, which lack supersymmetry and thus cannot rely on its protections to ensure accuracy. We investigate these theoretical models using large-N methods, sigma-meson analyses, and by computing three-loop amplitudes to assess their validity. While our results offer a robust confirmation of established supersymmetric dualities, they additionally identify one non-supersymmetric duality that appears fully consistent across every verification method; this validates recent predictions made by Hořava and Minwalla. In contrast, the study determines that three other non-supersymmetric duality proposals are fundamentally incorrect based on our evidence.

Let $\mathcal R$ denote a finite commutative ring with unity, and consider a linear code $\mathcal C$ as an $\mathcal R$-submodule of $\mathcal R^n$. This work investigates the properties of $\mathcal C$'s complements, specifically addressing conditions under which $\mathcal C$ admits a complement, defining the dual code $\mathcal C^\perp$, and establishing criteria for $\mathcal C$ to be perfectly complementary (i.e., $\mathcal C^\perp = \mathcal C^\perp$). Furthermore, we establish bounds on the sizes of $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal C^\perp$ without requiring them to be equal, thereby generalizing findings related to binary linear codes. These results are illustrated with examples drawn from $\mathcal C$ codes over the ring $\mathcal Z_9$.

This paper introduces a novel representation for discrete functions that enables faster exact inference in graphical models. We illustrate its utility in two primary areas: first, accelerating the solution of the constrained optimisation problem associated with constrained maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation; and second, speeding up the computation of the exact minimum expected penalty (mEP) for a custom-defined penalty.

This study introduces a novel asynchronous audio-visual (AV) fallen object detection task, where the objective is to pinpoint the location of a dropped item using only visual imagery and the signal that the object's impact occurred, without specifying exactly when it happened. This flexibility in timing is crucial for real-world applications such as identifying meals left on dining tables by elderly individuals or garbage abandoned on streets. The proposed methodology employs two core components: 1) an attention-based representation that aligns visual features with the most probable moments of the fall within the AV signal, and 2) the utilization of contrastive loss to enhance the discriminative power of learned features. The dataset was constructed by syncing fall detection audio with naturalistic video footage from the M25-700k benchmark. Extensive experiments demonstrate that this approach significantly improves upon current baselines, achieving an accuracy of 80.0%. The resulting open-source resources, including the dataset and code, are available at https://github.com/zhengzheng1999/FallDetection.

Discontinuous shear thickening (ST) represents a dramatic increase in viscosity within concentrated suspensions when subjected to high shear rates. In this study, we examine the rapid shear ST transitions occurring in three distinct colloidal systems, utilizing rheological measurements and high-speed imaging. By analyzing the scaling of yield stress as a function of particle concentration, we observe a universal scaling behavior across all three suspensions, which is governed by the ST amplitude exponent of 21. Furthermore, our findings indicate that rapid shear ST transitions in concentrated suspensions result from a dual mechanism: a contact friction-driven process and a dilute particle contribution.

This study examines power consumption patterns during crises, utilizing data from the 2021 Texas event. We employ a dynamic regression model featuring trigonometric terms to represent time, a method that captures both daily cycles and seasonal variations. The findings indicate that the crisis results in only minor fluctuations in consumption relative to normal times, with peak usage occurring during the afternoon hours.

Personalization in web search often results in users receiving distinct result sets, potentially causing them to overlook pertinent information hidden within links they are less likely to visit. We conducted a laboratory experiment involving 100 participants who evaluated search outcomes for 20 queries under both personalized and non-personalized conditions. We assessed personalization effects using a randomized control group receiving identical results for all queries. Results indicate that personalization reduced task effectiveness by 13% and decreased rating consistency among participants by 23%. Furthermore, personalization altered results in a way that increased diversity of opinions but reduced overall accuracy.

Automating the creation of programming code is a longstanding research objective aimed at assisting less skilled developers. This paper introduces GRCNN, a novel end-to-end architecture designed to synthesize programming code directly from flowchart images. GRCNN employs a dual parallel network structure: the first converts image data into a weighted graph representing the diagram's logical topology, while the second utilizes graph convolutional operations on this weighted network to generate linear sequences of programming code. We established a comprehensive dataset comprising 1,000 flowchart images and their corresponding AutoHotkey scripts to facilitate model training and evaluation. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art methods, achieving an F1 score of 0.70.

We examine various methods of dimension reduction applied to idealized models within idealized climate modeling, specifically focusing on equatorial dynamics, the quasi-geostrophic regime, and stochastic forcing. In the case of an equatorial dynamics model under periodic boundary conditions, the reduction to normal forms reveals the emergence of stochastic limit cycles when subjected to stochastic noise. Similarly, the application of center-manifold reduction to a model exhibiting quasi-geostrophic behavior in horizontal periodicity and stochastic vertical forcing demonstrates horizontal turbulence generation driven by injected energy. Finally, the discussion outlines reduction strategies for Stochastic Differential Equations (SDEs) and their corresponding partial differential equation (PDE) counterparts, addressing both the theoretical and statistical implications of these approaches for both pure mathematicians and climate scientists.

The formation of black holes and neutron stars, as well as the creation of heavy elements, occurs through mergers of compact objects. These events, or kilonas, emit light across the electromagnetic spectrum, with opacity in the visible range being particularly crucial for interpreting their observed signals. This study utilizes the OPACITY code to analyze opacity in the visible spectrum for electron densities ranging from $10^{-4}$ to $10^{10}$ g cm$^{-3}$ and temperatures between 0.03 eV and 10 eV, specifically within the atomic species Os, Pt, Hg, Au, and Ir. These calculations employ a fine-structure relativistic configuration interaction method, yielding energy levels, transition probabilities, and opacity coefficients. The resulting opacity data are intended to support future empirical studies of kilonas.

This paper details an approach to segmenting stomach anatomical regions utilizing deep learning techniques. It begins with a review of existing methods and current research trends in automated segmentation, followed by a description of using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) as the core model. The study employs the U-Net architecture, trained on MRI datasets from 100 Japanese individuals to handle segmentation tasks. Post-processing steps refine the initial predictions to improve accuracy, ultimately achieving an Intersection over Union (IoU) score of 0.935 and a Dice coefficient of 0.950.

Compositional data are characterized by a fixed total, meaning their components are interdependent rather than independent, which renders standard statistical techniques invalid. This study provides a fundamental introduction to the assessment of compositional data, demonstrating how linear algebra and visual analysis—specifically through logs ratios and simplexes—can be employed to investigate their unique properties. We also outline standard practices for handling missing values and scaling issues, illustrated using a real-world example concerning the structural assessment of food items' nutritional content.

The search for exoplanets with masses between Neptune and Saturn has been a major focus of the field for over twenty years, yet the discovery rate for such objects has remained surprisingly low. This study utilizes the CORALIE/HARPS radial velocity dataset to analyze the current status of sub-Neptune-to-sub-Saturn mass planets. We examine 100 stars with spectral types ranging from F8 to K2, using a dataset of 10,000 spectral measurements to fit 1,000 stars with 1,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,

Biological agents possess innate mechanisms to regulate their attention, yet the precise neural strategies underlying this regulation remain unclear. This research proposes a biological model for attention control grounded in the principle of mutual information maximization, utilizing an abstract visual agent navigating a structured environment. Our findings indicate that mutual information-driven attention effectively enhances learning efficiency and attentional allocation. When applied to noisy input conditions, a robust variant of this mechanism demonstrates superior performance compared to alternative regulated strategies, successfully avoiding the propagation of noise to the agent's internal state. This robust system also maintains consistent attentional focus on salient environmental features, thereby reducing unnecessary computational resources. Ultimately, the proposed mutual information-based framework offers a plausible blueprint for how structured attention regulation develops in natural agents.

We investigate the interaction of dark matter (DM) with baryons, which results in significant DM density enhancements within galactic cores. Our findings indicate that even when this interaction involves spin-independent scattering off nucleons, terrestrial direct detection experiments possess sufficient sensitivity to constrain the parameter space. We examine how this phenomenology alters previous constraints on Yukuwa-mediated forces between DM and visible matter, ultimately demonstrating that such forces can exist in regimes where gravity alone cannot account for observed stellar motions in galaxies.

Recent years have seen significant progress in cognitive neuroscience, yet progress in AI remains hindered by limitations in current neural network architectures. Inspired by the brain's biological structure, the human cortex comprises sparse neural populations where individual neurons rarely activate, a property that appears to facilitate rapid learning. This study demonstrates that artificial Neural Random Projections (RNNs), when constrained to maintain similar sparse connectivity and activity levels found in the biological cortex, also benefit from this sparsity. Specifically, these sparse RNNs utilize fixed, shared sparse projection layers, eliminating the need for any learnable parameters. By applying this architecture to diverse cognitive tasks, we found that keeping learning rates low and ensuring internal network sparity accelerates the acquisition process. Consequently, enforcing these biological constraints on many tasks not only speeds up learning but also boosts final performance, often surpassing that achieved by fully dense recurrent models.

This paper categorizes nilpotent graded commutative algebra algebras based on their graded Hilbert series, with all results applying mutatis mutandis to the non- commutative setting as well. Specifically, we demonstrate that such an algebra $A$ is isomorphic to a skew-quotient of an exterior algebra $\Omega$ modulo a vector space of degree $d$ relations, $I/(x_1^2, \dots, x_n^2)$, where the $d$-graded components of $I$ vanish unless they are generated by $d$-quadratic terms. This classification extends to cases where $A$ is a quotient of a polynomial algebra $k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ modulo an ideal $I/(x_1^{n+1}, \dots, x_n^{n+1})$, where the $d$-graded components of $I$ vanish unless they are generated by $n

Radio-loud active galactic nuclei (AGNs) release powerful jets that can expand into the intergalactic medium (IGM). When these jets reach the IGM, they generate radio bubbles and, eventually, radio galaxies. This study examines how the cosmic microwave background (CMB) influences the dynamical evolution of such jets, specifically focusing on the early epoch where the IGM density exceeds the CMB density. We developed a numerical model to track jet dynamics and calculated the resulting radio bubbles within the IGM. Our results indicate that the CMB significantly affects the expansion of jets around a redshift of $z \sim 10$. Consequently, the radio luminosity of the jets declines during this era, whereas their bolometric luminosity remains largely unaffected. We also estimated the radio luminosity of the jets and the associated radio galaxies throughout cosmic history.

We introduce Lagrangian formulations derived from a class of non-cinetic gravities proposed recently by two of the authors (AR). This framework allows for the systematic expansion of the theory up to quadratic order in spatial gradients of the scalar degree of freedom, enabling the computation of the speed of cosmological perturbations. We identify sub-classes within this large theoretical space that yield closed-form expressions valid to all orders regarding spatial gradients. Furthermore, we examine the potential of this broad lagrangian space by assessing gravities capable of addressing the Cosmological Constant problem.

This paper introduces a new general-purpose, fully automatic method for registering multi-channel medical image volumes, such as CT and MRI data. The proposed pipeline utilizes two distinct local feature-based techniques: the initial stage detects image features and matches them across channels, while the second stage refines the registration by precisely aligning matched features using 3D rotational symmetry operators. These operators, classified as Signal Processing (SP) symmetries, are derived from the discrete classification of 3D rotational rotations. The final alignment is achieved through an iterative, closed-form solution that minimizes registration error. Experimental validation on both simulated data and real clinical scans demonstrates that this approach significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of registration precision and computational speed.

We report the discovery of SDSS J082239.54+304857.19, a binary system composed of two white dwarfs orbiting with a period of 40.5 minutes. Analysis of its photometric light curves reveals a double-peaked eclipsing pattern, where the secondary eclipse is notably fainter than the primary. Spectroscopic data indicate a radial velocity semi-amplitude of $K_1 = 1030 \pm 10$ km s$^{-1}$ for the primary star and $i = 81 \pm 1^\circ$ for the orbital inclination. Combining these measurements with the orbital period yields derived masses of $M_1 = 0.53 \pm 0.03 M_\odot$ and $M_2 = 0.10 \pm 0.02 M_\odot$, along with an estimated radius of $R_1 = 0.031 \pm 0.002 R_\odot$. The light curve morphology suggests that the system is viewed nearly edge-on, with the primary white dwarf completely eclipsing the secondary. Furthermore, the light curve features exhibit characteristics consistent with the presence of a companion tilted relative to the orbital plane, likely caused by a circumstellar disc. This system stands as the second known double-degenerate binary featuring a white dwarf larger than $0.1 R_\

Global pooling layers are essential components in convolutional neural networks, yet their behavior remains poorly understood. This study investigates these layers by modeling them as solving an optimal transport problem with a specific cost function. This analytical framework reveals a connection to the spectral properties of convolution kernels, suggesting that transport costs between image patches drive global pooling efficacy. This insight offers criteria for evaluating pooling performance and guides the creation of a novel, transport-based global pooling architecture. Experimental results demonstrate that this new proposal surpasses current state-of-the-art methods on image classification benchmarks.

We examine the morphological characteristics of host galaxies surrounding active galactic nuclei (AGN) across different classifications, utilizing the SDSS DR12 sample. Our study targets 1,000,000 galaxies with redshifts below 0.05, selecting 1,000 examples from each AGN type (Radio, Radio QSO, Radio Galaxy, Seyfert 1, Seyfert 2, LINER, and Composite) to mitigate selection bias. Using the Galaxy Zoo visual classification database, we assessed host morphology and orientation. Findings indicate that radio AGN predominantly reside in early-type galaxies, whereas non-radio AGN are mostly found in late-type galaxies. Visual analysis reveals radio AGN are situated in more edge-on systems compared to non-radio AGN, which favor face-on orientations. These results support the orientation-dependent unification model, suggesting that the primary distinction between radio and non-radio AGN lies in the viewing angle of their jets.

This paper examines flat rotational surfaces subject to a pointwise 1-Gaussian map of point type within 4-dimensional space. We provide an analytical demonstration that such surfaces must be rotational cones or flat cylinders, thereby resolving an open question raised by B.-Y. Chen. Furthermore, we characterize a specific rotational surface with a non-vanessical Gaussian map under these advanced constraints.

Pre-training is a common strategy to enhance semantic segmentation performance, yet existing methods often rely on techniques that only marginally improve outcomes. This study explores leveraging unsupervised monocular depth estimation as a pre-training step. The process involves aligning depth predictions from this estimation with ground-plane depth maps to force the model to learn accurate scene geometry representations. Testing on the Cityscapes dataset demonstrates that this approach surpasses conventional pre-training methods, yielding an approximate 2% relative improvement in mean Intersection over Union (mIoU). The best model achieved a mIoU of 79.1% and a reduction in segmentation error by approximately 13%. Additionally, the research examines how different metric learning metrics influence the optimization process during pre-training.

Time-series data is ubiquitous across numerous fields, yet current methods for converting sequences into natural language narratives are restricted to specific domains, resulting in a lack of generalization. This paper introduces **TCube**, a large-scale, domain-general dataset containing 11,500 time-series examples drawn from three distinct fields: medicine, energy, and transportation. The data comprises paired sequences (ranging from 10 to 100 steps) and corresponding natural language descriptions, where each series includes at least one event and the descriptions explicitly mention it. To address this, we propose **SeqToStory**, a neural network architecture designed to map these natural language time-series narratives. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our model significantly surpasses strong baselines, improving ROUGE scores by over 20%. Furthermore, we offer a rigorous analysis of the dataset and the proposed task, including the introduction of **n-mention metrics** for evaluating the quality of described mentions.

Specific findings include ATLAS observations of the $B_s^0 \to \mu^+\mu^-$ decay, which establishes the $s_0$ term. We examine the Ising model on a Cayley tree within a magnetic field, establishing the existence of non-translation-invariant Gibbs states that exhibit a one-dimensional periodic structure of any arbitrary period $l \in \mathbb{N} \setminus \{1\}$. For specific parameter values, it is shown that magnetization curves corresponding to these states lack smoothness (are non-differentiable).

This paper examines a family of hyperbolic systems defined by $u_{tt} = (a(|\nabla u_t|) |\nabla u_t) + F(u_t, u, x, t)$, where the coefficients $a$ and source term $F$ exhibit at most logarithmic growth with respect to the gradient magnitude $|\zeta|$. For the initial-boundary value problem (IBVP) and Cauchy problem (CP) cases, we establish global well-posedness under the constraint that the $H^s$ norms of the initial data remain uniformly bounded for $s > d/2 + 2$. Furthermore, we derive uniform-in-time $C^{2,\alpha}$ regularity for the time derivative of the solution, $u_t$. These findings rely heavily on novel a priori estimates for the $W^{1,\infty}$ norm of $u_t$ and the $W^{s,\infty}$ norm of $u$.

Term segmentation involves separating sequences of words into meaningful terms, a critical task in information retrieval. This study introduces a novel approach for segmenting terms in Japanese using a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) framework. By leveraging Japanese Word Segmentation Corpora, the research demonstrates that this method outperforms existing systems and vector space models. Furthermore, the resulting system, which surpasses current state-of-the-art performance, is released as open-source.

This paper presents a results-based exploratory study examining external links shared within the Community of Stack Overflow (SO). Our investigation centers on the frequency of these connections, the variety of linked domains, and the characteristics of the users who post them. We also analyze shared links from an temporal perspective, observing patterns across weekdays, holidays, and over extended periods. Furthermore, we examine the nature of the content from specific domains, such as Wikipedia, that are contributed to the platform.

Galactic diversity is a vital yet unresolved issue in astronomy. Current simulations fail to replicate the observed variety in galaxy properties, particularly regarding star formation rates, gas fractions, and morphological structures. This study critically reviews proposed solutions to this problem, emphasizing the role of supermassive black hole (SMBH) feedback. While widely regarded as a primary mechanism for regulating galaxy evolution, the specific nature of SMBH feedback remains debated. We examine various models involving jets, shocks, and outflows, and review recent hydrodynamical simulations that incorporate these elements. Despite significant advancements, current simulations still struggle to match the full breadth of the observed galaxy diversity problem.

The escalating climate crisis demands public discourse to shift from debate to constructive discourse aimed at implementing effective mitigation strategies. To facilitate this, we introduce CKBase, the first comprehensive knowledge base dedicated to climate science, designed to support question-answering systems and other information technologies. By enabling access to reliable, accurate data, it helps users form well-informed opinions and engage in meaningful dialogue regarding climate science. Building on existing structured resources, we expanded coverage by integrating detailed information regarding impacts, causes, and responses to climate change. This expansion involved extracting data from over 1.5 million abstracts across more than 100 specialized journals within the climate research landscape. We further developed advanced retrieval mechanisms to ensure seamless user interaction. Ultimately, CKBase offers a robust foundation for various information systems, including those tailored for general public use.

Symptom extraction from clinical text is vital for multi-task clinical Natural Language Processing (NLP) yet remains difficult due to domain-specific linguistic variations. This study addresses symptom negative event extraction, which involves identifying symptoms present only in their neglated form (e.g., "no fever"). While essential for patient safety, existing models trained on isolated domains fail to generalize across different settings. To tackle this, the authors introduce a new large-scale, dual-domain dataset comprising 10,000 annotated negative clinical notes from two sources, MIMIC-III and US National Discharge Dataset (NDD). Leveraging this resource, the authors propose a domain-general negative event extraction framework that integrates (1) a dual-domain pre-training phase using BERT-based part-of-speech guidance and (2) a domain-adversarial fine-tuning method. Evaluated against three domains and a base model, the proposed system demonstrates significant improvements, outperforming previous approaches by 10.4% in dual-domain settings and achieving 10.4% to 14.8% gains across three specific domains relative to a standard baseline. The code and annotations are publicly available at https://github.com/rohit-rajput/negative-event-extraction.

In the field of autonomous driving, deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has emerged as a prominent research area. This paper introduces a new DRL system designed to train a driver agent within a specific environment. The work begins by examining the fundamental principles of DRL and its relevance to self-driving technology. It then details the system's architecture, which utilizes the MAZU autonomous driving framework as a basis. By employing a simplified environment representation, our approach achieves efficient training with reduced computational costs. Furthermore, we have developed a state-of-the-art neural network architecture that represents both the vehicle's state and the driver, demonstrating superior performance when compared to existing methods.

This study introduces a precise yet energy-efficient classification approach utilizing a continuous neural network with random weights, eliminating the need for backpropagation. By applying theoretical analysis of continuous neural networks, we derive the optimal distribution for weight initialization to maximize the Cramér–Rao lower bound. This continuous model is subsequently adapted to neural networks utilizing discrete spikes. Empirical results on four benchmark datasets demonstrate that this method achieves high accuracy and, in the case of the CIFAR-10 dataset, reduces the number of neurons by 40% compared to existing techniques. Furthermore, the model exhibits robust generalization capabilities, remaining effective despite significant variations in learning rates and batch sizes.

In this study, we investigate the properties of spin-polarized strange quark matter under extreme conditions, specifically within high temperatures and intense external magnetic fields. Our analysis examines the equation of state alongside the macroscopic characteristics of this form of strange star, evaluating their dependence on temperature and magnetic field strength as well as the system's net spin polarization. Our findings indicate that increasing temperature significantly alters the state of the strange quark matter, whereas the external magnetic field exerts only a negligible impact on these properties.

This paper introduces Pando, a personal assistant designed to operate within web browsers alongside a user's specific profile. By leveraging the non-biased, transparent data access of the browser environment, Pando mitigates concerns surrounding privacy and data security while providing continuous, long-term support. The system is built upon the User Model, which maintains persistent user data, and the Activity Model, which records historical interactions to refine the model's accuracy. Pando employs a multi-agent architecture to balance effective collaboration with autonomous operation. To validate the system, researchers conducted a 12-week, real-world pilot study involving 10 participants who used Pando integrated with their Google services. The findings demonstrate that the system successfully adapts to individual users and offers tangible assistance, thereby supporting user goals and enhancing overall efficiency.

We introduce a robust technique for approximating the nonlinear spectral properties of a class of nonlinear operators. The method is grounded in minimal rational interpolation (MRI) applied to a vector of rational evaluations of the Fréchet derivative at various grid points. Under the assumption that the derivative varies smoothly across the domain, MRI generates a Ritz-based eigenvalue problem that offers a computationally efficient approximation. Furthermore, the approach delivers an asymptotically optimal asymptotic convergence rate for smooth solution types.

We demonstrate that every intermediate $\beta$-shift is weakly equivalent to a greedy greedy $= \beta$-shift with a gap. As a consequence of this finding, the category of weak equivalence for intermediate shifts is fully determined by a single parameter representing the gap. Consequently, every such system possessing a gap exhibits a factorization into a commuting pair consisting of a gap $= \beta$-shift and a strictly less than or equal to the given ground $= \beta

We present the inaugural numerical lattice gauge theory simulations utilizing even $SO(N_c)$ gauge groups that demonstrate both confinement and the breaking of chiral symmetry within $SO(N_c)$ gauge theories coupled with $N_f$ fermion doublets in three dimensions. This simulation employs a fermion determinant-based approach for $N_f \leq 2$, achieving a breakdown of chiral symmetry as evidenced by a reduction in Polyakov loop degeneracy and a mass ratio between light quark axial and vector mesons. These findings substantiate that $N_f=1$ functions as a viable non-asymptotically free matter content capable of triggering dynamical electroweak symmetry breaking, a scenario that remains inaccessible to perturbative methods.

We present a new method for decoding the behavior of Random Forest models and other tree ensemble structures by decomposing them into conceptually distinct components, specifically utilizing Disentangled Attribution Curves (DAC). Our approach breaks down decision trees by isolating the contribution of each split, allowing these splits to be categorized based on whether they function as "hard" filters that exclude data, "soft" filters that proportionally reduce weights, or act as leaf nodes preserving information. Consequently, we derive enhanced explanations for the original model by constructing DACs, which visualize how a given input traces through an estimated ensemble. Compared to existing techniques, our methodology offers a more granular layer of granularity by distinguishing between hard and soft decisions, and we validate the efficacy of these explanations using a range of synthetic and real-world datasets.

Federated Learning (FL) offers a robust framework for training machine learning models on distributed, privacy-conscious data. FL protocols are designed to maintain data privacy by ensuring that sensitive information, such as dataset contents and model weights, remains undisclosed during the communication process. However, existing FL systems face limitations: they either require all parties to pre-install specific software on their devices, imposing trust on the output of shared code, or depend on a semi-trusted central server that can access local data, creating vulnerabilities during data transfer. To overcome these barriers, we introduce "Flatee," a novel, fully trusted-free FL architecture. Flatee leverages Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) on individual devices to create a secure, decentralized coordination layer. This approach eliminates the need for any single party to trust others or a central infrastructure, allowing Flatee to function without central access to local data. The Flatee system operates by establishing a graph-based communication topology where TEEs on each device jointly compute consensus for model updates through coordinated, encrypted operations. We demonstrate the efficacy of Flatee by implementing state-of-the-art gradient consensus algorithms for deep neural networks, successfully applying them to two benchmark datasets. Experimental results confirm that Flatee achieves competitive model accuracy and demonstrates resilience against various attacks and faulty nodes.

As autonomous driving technology advances, the need for a rigorous evaluation framework is also increasing. This system evaluates drivers based on safety, comfort, and efficiency, offering an objective benchmark to compare different drivers and evaluate autonomous system performance. While current methodologies employ quantitative and qualitative metrics to assess driving behavior, the challenge remains in efficiently and accurately calculating these metrics. Although existing solutions utilize camera and sensor data for metric assessment, they typically involve complex metric-specific algorithms that are difficult to deploy on small embedded systems with limited resources. This paper introduces a novel metric-based approach that enables the efficient computation of driving metrics within these constrained environments.

Autonomous Policy Learning (APL) represents a cutting-edge method for addressing policy issues in sequential decision-making, yet its application within policy learning for resource management remains unexplored. This study introduces Timeloops, a novel framework designed to learn system call policies for microservices running in containerized environments. Timeloops employs deep reinforcement learning to optimize the mapping between system requests and microservice allocations, aiming to maximize long-term rewards. The learning process involves simulating policy executions, evaluating outcomes, and refining the policy based on these results. The derived policies are implemented via an interface compatible with major microservice frameworks, including Spring Boot and Node.js. Empirical results demonstrate that Timeloops significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art approaches in achieving higher system utilization, enhanced request processing rates, and a reduction in queue lengths.

This study examines linear classifiers within the three-dimensional forms of merchandise, utilizing the merchandise description from a single-word tag in an auto-encoder-based feature space. The classifiers were evaluated on two datasets: a tagged collection of three-dimensional forms of merchandise and a set of three-dimensional forms of merchandise found on Amazon. The evaluation process involved assessing the classifiers' performance by comparing their rankings against human-identified categories of three-dimensional forms of merchandise. The findings reveal that these three-dimensional forms of merchandise are not only more effective than traditional image-based features but also demonstrate a higher degree of interpretability.

We investigate the spatial distribution of stars surrounding a central supermassive black hole (BH) within a galactic nucleus. The specific stellar population under study is one where stars possess sufficiently high mutual separations to prevent their collective gravitational effects from altering the BH's mass measurement. The analysis focuses on two limiting scenarios: a strong separation regime where interactions are negligible, and a weak separation regime where they are significant. In the strong separation context, we derive the stellar density profile, $\eta(r)$, for a system confined by a potential well of power-law index $\gamma$ (where $\eta(r) \propto r^{-3\gamma/2}$). This derivation assumes a constant specific energy distribution, $\eta(E) = \text{const}$, applicable to systems with isotropic velocity dispersion. The strong separation model is subsequently extended to cases with arbitrary velocity dispersion. In the weak separation limit, we demonstrate that $\eta(r)$ transitions to $r^{-5}$ as the potential index $\gamma$ increases beyond $2.5$. Furthermore, we analyze how $\eta(r)$ evolves with $\gamma$ in the strong separation limit and find that stellar clusters with steeper density profiles are more susceptible to dynamical interactions. The findings indicate that while the strong separation assumption is valid for nuclei with shallow potentials, conditions shift in deep potential wells, where stellar interactions become a critical factor.

This paper introduces a novel probabilistic model predictive control (PMPC) framework designed to incorporate probabilistic constraints alongside probabilistic predictions of system dynamics. The proposed formulation is resolved through a technique combining scenario sampling with an approximation of Value Functions, representing the first application of this specific methodology to PMPC problems. We provide sufficient conditions that ensure path-wise convergence of the control trajectory as both the number of scenarios and prediction horizon extend toward infinity. The effectiveness of the suggested approach, including a comparison with standard MPC, is demonstrated through a simulation study.

Compressive Sensing (CS) has emerged as a powerful strategy for acquiring and reconstructing high-dimensional signals, enabling the reduction of measurement counts below the Nyquist limit through exploitation of sparsity in specific bases. While existing CS methods effectively recover signals when basis complexity remains low, they struggle significantly as the underlying sparsity basis dimension grows prohibitively large. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a novel Compressive Sensing framework designed to address Multi-Singular-Operator data characterized by inherent low-rank structures. Our proposed Compressive Singular Component Analysis (CS-SCA) decomposes these datasets into distinct components: a principal singular value representing overall magnitude, and additional singular vectors that define spatial patterns. Beyond proposing a solid algorithmic foundation, we rigorously derive the necessary conditions and provide theoretical proofs regarding the required measurement count to guarantee successful decomposition. Furthermore, we validate the efficacy of the methodology across diverse scenarios, demonstrating its substantial advantages in demanding applications such as Compressed Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI).

In a noise-modulated elector model featuring two competing species, the dynamics of species distribution are governed by a competition-colonization tradeoff. The first species is superior in direct competition for resources but relies on electors to access the remainder of the domain, whereas the second species possesses lower competitive efficiency but can utilize a broader range of habitats due to higher elector density extending further. A key parameter determines the existence of a unique steady state, resulting in the exclusion of the second species, versus enabling multiple steady states where both species coexist. This coexistence manifests as a heterogeneous spatial pattern characterized by a uniform elector distribution interspersed with localized clusters of the second species. Furthermore, under a regime of localized electors, the system transitions to either a single homogeneous state, implying total elector disappearance and the dominance of only the first species, or several states featuring widespread colonization by the second species across most elector-rich zones alongside the initial species.

In the long-range Ising model, excitations are classified as either visons or anyons. Within the context of the 3D quantum double model, similar excitation categories have been identified. This study investigates a cluster of local von Neumann alims—specifically those with a finite second split spectrum in an 3-d quantum double model that exhibits anyonic excitations. Our findings reveal a striking parallel between these algebra categories and the ones defined by visons in the long-range Ising model.

We investigate a coherent feedback control scheme designed to enhance the rate of three-way entanglement involving magnon, photon, and phonon degrees of freedom within cavity magnomechanics. Our findings demonstrate that the proposed feedback mechanism significantly boosts both the emergent magnon-phonon and full magnon-photon-phonon entanglement. Specifically, when compared to a standard linear coupling setup, the coherent signal amplification achieved through this feedback increases the two-component entanglement rate by a factor of 100 and the three-component rate by 1000. These performance gains stem from the ability of the feedback loop to simultaneously strengthen magnon-photon coupling and reduce dissipation rates associated with phonons and magnons. Consequently, this approach facilitates the establishment of robust, multi-variable correlations essential for emerging quantum information technologies.

We present a comprehensive set of NLO one-loop triple-collinear splitting matrix elements for all possible flavor combinations of partons within a dimensionally-regulated framework. These elements are derived from the corresponding tree-level expressions compiled in arXiv:1305.7187, which covered all double-collinear flavors, and are expressed as functions of loop momentum inlay. To facilitate their application, we also provide complete mapping tables that relate our results to the splitting pattern tables for both collinear and splintering limits found in arXiv:1503.04657.

The solution utilizes an iterative procedure that applies successive transformations, employing both standard and generalized versions of smooth operations. The article further provides examples of resolution for particular one-dimensional local rings characterized by $\mathbb C$-vector space parameters $m$ and $n$."

This paper introduces the **Suryakala-Nusantara** project, dedicated to documenting sundials across Indonesia. Drawing upon prior research by our team, we provide historical backgrounds for sundial timekeeping in the region and present initial findings from the study.

Next-generation wireless networks are expected to support the surging demand for data throughput and energy efficiency, a challenge that Device-to-Device (D2D) communication may help address by improving spectral efficiency and reducing transmission power. However, simultaneous data and energy harvesting using D2D links remains an underexplored area. This paper introduces a novel integrated framework that synergizes D2D communications with simultaneous wireless information and power (DWPP) reception. The objective is to maximize D2D throughput while ensuring a predefined minimum throughput for information receivers (IRs). To achieve this, we employ the cognitive radio paradigm, allowing D2D links to access information from information transmitters (ITs) and IRs. The proposed solution first determines the optimal transmit power for ITs and IRs, followed by deriving the optimal directionality for D2D transmitters using the Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB). Subsequently, we propose a decomposition-based algorithm to determine the optimal beamwidth for D2D transmitters. Finally, a low-complexity alternative is introduced to mitigate the high computational complexity of the initial high-precision approach.

This study introduces a novel approach for Distant Operation, enabling two-dimensional Laser Doppler Vibrometry (LDV) measurements from a single point. By integrating spatially resolved data from a high-speed camera with velocity data obtained via LDV, the system localizes the specific points of interest. This method was experimentally verified through the measurement of surface velocities around a targeted area on various objects during sinusoidal vibrations between 10 Hz and 1.5 kHz. The proposed technique significantly reduces both measurement time and the number of required probes compared to the conventional LDV method, which necessitates scanning multiple locations.

We demonstrate that any context-free language can be defined using first-order patterns with only binary relations. This finding extends prior work by Heuner and overcomes a limitation identified by Durand regarding duration constraints associated with temporal logic patterns.

Although modern TEMs typically include integrated aberration correctors, there is a growing interest in utilizing a programmable phase plate (PP) for both imaging and spectroscopy applications. This study investigates how a PP can effectively replace traditional systems, focusing on its capacity to dynamically modify astigmatism and chromatic aberration. Results indicate that a PP can introduce precise dynamic astigmatism corrections, with performance approaching that of a hexapole corrector. Furthermore, by manipulating the phase of an annular probe, a PP can mitigate chromatic aberration, achieving a theoretical limit of 0.5\(\mathring{A}\) probe size at a 1% height change. Ultimately, this research demonstrates that a PP offers a versatile, multi-functional alternative to conventional aberration correctors.

This study examines the relationship between the relationships between algorithmic complexity relative to assessment function complexity within assessment functions.
