The newly identified, isolated, and distant (z ≈ 0.04) young (≈ 10 Myr) brown dwarf WISEA J153429.75-104303.3, commonly referred to as "The Mishap," was initially thought to be a prime candidate for a comprehensive study of its atmospheric and physical characteristics. However, follow-up observations revealed that it is actually part of a wide binary system with a second brown dwarf companion, and its previously estimated age was significantly overestimated. Consequently, it is no longer considered a suitable subject for detailed atmospheric modeling. This article provides a full analysis of the system, including its spectral characteristics, atmospheric composition, physical parameters, and evolutionary status. We introduce an effective method for computing parton distribution functions that achieves significantly faster convergence by effectively resuming all logarithmic and power-like terms. This effective procedure is demonstrated through an application involving the DGLAP evolution of these distributions.

This study investigates how sintering temperature affects the microstructure and mechanical properties of pressed pellets made from Martian and lunar regolith simulants. We examined the phase composition and microstructure of the resulting pellets using XRD, SEM, and EDS. Furthermore, we evaluated their uniaxial compressive strength (UCS) and water absorption rates. The findings indicate that sintering at 1000°C yields optimal outcomes, where a glassy phase forms at the sand particle interfaces, significantly lowering water absorption and enhancing uniaxial compressive strength. These results underscore the critical role of sintering temperature in microstructural development and suggest that achieving a temperature of 1000°C is essential for producing high-quality regolith ceramics.

The surface mobility of a liquid film flowing over a cylindrical fiber is investigated. When the fiber rotates, the liquid experiences slip at the cylindrical interface, characterized by the Péclet number, which quantifies the ratio of convective to diffusive effects. This slip generates a secondary axial flow within the film, inducing additional radial pressure gradients that amplify the Rayleigh-Plateau instability. Consequently, this leads to faster growth of disturbances and shorter wavelengths. The study employs linear stability analysis to examine the initial development of these disturbances and demonstrates that increased convective transport intensifies the disturbance growth rate while decreasing period length. Furthermore, numerical simulations are conducted to model the evolution of the finite-amplitude instability, revealing slip-enhanced drop formation. These numerically produced droplets exhibit characteristics—specifically size and growth rate—that align well with analytical predictions.

The star formation rate (SFR) is a fundamental metric for characterizing a galaxy's evolution. While the infrared flux at 24 $\mu$m ($F_{24}$) is the standard method for estimating SFR in nearby galaxies, this approach relies on spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting, a technique that introduces significant uncertainties. To address these limitations, we propose utilizing the Brackett-$\gamma$ ($Br\gamma$) line flux as a robust alternative. We analyzed $Br\gamma$ data from the Spitzer Infrared Array Camera (IRAC) for 120 galaxies with known, reliable SFRs to validate this approach. Our findings indicate that the coefficient of determination ($R^2$) between $\log(\text{SFR})$ derived from $Br\gamma$ and that derived from $F_{24}$ is 0.98, compared to 0.94 for the original method. Furthermore, we developed a calibration specifically for $Br\gamma$ to calculate SFR, achieving a scatter of only 0.3 dex.

This article establishes the symmetries relevant to regional-type modules for integrable affine $I$ modules associated with $I$ series $\mathfrak{sl}_N$ (specifically $I$ series $\mathfrak{sl}_N$). We demonstrate that the Kashiwara operators, along with their associated "type $I$ quantum subgroup" (specifically $I$ series $\mathfrak{sl}_N$), can be constructed. This quantum subgroup enables the explicit computation of the action of Kashiwara operators on regional-type modules for $I$ series $\mathfrak{sl}_N$ through operations on "type $I$ quantum subgroup" (specifically $I$ series $\mathfrak{sl}_N$). This method leverages the correspondence between type $I$ quantum subgroup and type $I$ quantum subgroup (specifically $I$ series $\mathfrak{sl}_N$). As a result, we obtain a "type $I$ quantum subgroup" (specifically $I$ series $\mathfrak{sl}_N$) (specifically $I$ series $\mathfrak{sl}_N$). Furthermore, we derive a "type $I$ quantum subgroup" (specifically $I$ series $\mathfrak{sl}_N$).

This paper introduces a new method for solving equations related to the General Diffusion Process (GDP). Under specific conditions, we demonstrate that our proposed scheme achieves second-order accuracy in the $L^2$ norm and any order of accuracy in $H^{-m}$ norm. Furthermore, we develop a direct approach to compute the variable step size step.

Optical character recognition (OCR) is a well-established method for identifying printed text, yet it struggles with cursive handwriting, especially in complex domains like mathematics. This study introduces a deep learning-driven system that identifies handwritten mathematical expressions by analyzing temporal sensor data. The system's performance was evaluated on a dataset of 1,000 distinct binary features representing 1,000 unique expressions. The data was split into training, validation, and testing sets comprising 60%, 20%, and 20% of the data, respectively. The model was built using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) trained on this time-series data. The system achieved an accuracy of 81.1% in classifying the expressions, demonstrating that temporal features captured by the sensor are effective for recognition tasks where OCR fails.

This study introduces a new method for estimating speech duration in median-based, non-parametric analysis. The proposed approach is parametric-free and utilizes the median to model speech signal characteristics, with a specific focus on analyzing the median of phoneme durations. The formulation analyzes how the median of aggregated data relates to the medians of underlying constituent data groups. By applying this principle, the research establishes a data-driven, closed-form equation estimating phoneme duration. The suggested equation represents an estimation derived from recorded individual phoneme durations. The methodology was validated using the University of Edinburgh's CMU Arctic speech database. Results demonstrate that this proposed formula yields highly accurate estimates, achieving a correlation coefficient of 0.999 with measured phoneme durations.

Spatial presence models are increasingly utilized in ecological research to analyze species distribution data while accounting for spatial autocorrelation. The **spOccupancy** package is designed to fit these models using binary presence/absence data, whether for single species or integrated into multi-species and integrated analysis frameworks. In this article, we describe the package's features and functions, introduce novel methodologies, and provide illustrative examples based on simulated data and practical datasets.

The Skincare initiative is a deep learning project dedicated to detecting and diagnosing skin lesions. It employs a hybrid approach combining automatic methods, such as interactive deep learning, with semi-automatic techniques, including medical image analysis and recommendation systems. A distinctive feature of Skincare is its use of an interactive deep learning module that assists physicians by suggesting probable dermatological diagnoses, thereby reducing user burden and enhancing diagnostic accuracy. This system operates by ranking potential diagnoses to guide clinical decision-making, a capability evaluated using a modified area under the curve metric, ranked-ROC (rROC). During the initial R&D phase, the ranking performance achieved an rROC score of 0.935. In subsequent public demonstrations, the system's ranking accuracy improved to an rROC of 0.955.

We introduce a probabilistic autoencoder designed to forecast future spectra for Type Ia supernovae utilizing current and historical spectral data. This approach models data uncertainty by integrating a normal likelihood function with fully localized latent representations. By leveraging short-term spectral dynamics, the system predicts future states, with performance validated against the SNLS3 dataset.

We present deep, multi-band imaging and spectroscopy of COSMOS-C042. S, a lensed dusty star-forming galaxy located at z = 2.09, which reveals a resolved neutral outflow spanning 2.5 kpc with a maximum velocity of 1,000 km s$^{-1}$. This outflow exhibits a bipolar morphology, displaying a pronounced velocity gradient from -1,000 km s$^{-1}$ in the redshifted (east) direction to +1,000 km s$^{-1}$ in the blueshifted (west) direction. The outflow's kinematics are modeled as a single rotating disk viewed nearly edge-on, with a best-fit inclination of 87.1° ± 0.1°. We detect a significant correlation between outflow velocity and position within the galaxy, suggesting a mechanical driving mechanism. The outflow's mass is estimated at 1,000 ± 200 M$_{\odot}$, representing a mass-loading factor of 1.1 ± 0.2 relative to the galaxy's star-formation rate. Furthermore, the outflow's momentum far exceeds that of the galaxy's interstellar radiation field, indicating that radiation pressure is insufficient to explain the observed gas motion.

Entrainment within particle-laden turbulent plumes is investigated through numerical simulations, employing a novel subgrid-scale model for momentum fluxes developed specifically for particle-filled turbulent flows. The examined scenario involves the developing turbulent buoyant plume generated by a hot, particle-containing source situated in a quiescent environment. Simulation results indicate that the presence of solid particles significantly alters the entrainment dynamics of the plume. Specifically, when particles exhibit negative buoyancy, both the plume's momentum and its entrainment rate are suppressed; conversely, negatively accelerated plumes with neutrally buoyant particles display an enhanced entrainment rate. The study attributes this augmentation to an intensification of turbulent fluctuations and the emergence of an additional entrainment mechanism driven by particle clustering.

The propagation of infectious diseases within social networks is a subject of significant interest, driven by the goal of refining epidemic forecasting and control strategies. While extensive research has focused on networks, this work investigates the extinction dynamics of infectious diseases in a more realistic framework: hypergraphs, where multiple social interactions can occur simultaneously. We introduce a rigorous spectral methodology to establish precise spectral lower bounds regarding the basic reproduction number ($R_0$)—a pivotal metric indicating whether an epidemic will surge or subside. Our findings demonstrate a profound connection between $R_0$ and the second-largest eigenvalue of a specific self-adjoint operator derived from the hypergraph's structure. Furthermore, we provide spectral upper bounds to determine the precise threshold at which an epidemic outbreak becomes unsustainable. By extending previous research, our contribution offers a deeper spectral understanding of outbreak dynamics in complex, multi-simultaneous interaction scenarios.

The turn-on of magnetic exchange in CrI$_3$ monolayers, which are known I-VI monolayer ferromagnets, enables the emergence of a tunable two-dimensional Rashba effect. This study investigates the spin textures of such centro-symmetric I-VI monolayers, specifically focusing on the dual influences of the finite magnetization and the Rashba effect. Our results show that while spin textures are generally blocked by saturation magnetization, finite Rashba coupling disrupts this blockade, generating characteristic "half-moon" patterns. Using time-dependent density functional theory (DFT) and the Kohn-Sham eigenstates of a Rashba model, we examined the spin properties of CrI$_3$ bilayers. We found that out-of-plane magnetization yields half-moon textures with spins oriented radially, whereas in-plane magnetization produces textures with moons-shaped spins aligned along the tangent. These experimental signatures can be identified via spin-polarized scanning tunneling microscopy (SP-STM).

The standard model of solar differential rotation features a prograde, latitude-dependent angular velocity profile, peaking at the tachocline and declining toward the equator. In contrast, many solar-like stars exhibit a "anti-solar" profile, where angular velocity increases with depth but decreases toward lower latitudes. We investigated the dynamical effects of this anti-solar profile using mean-field magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) simulations. Our findings indicate that despite the absence of global shear, these systems can sustain magnetic cycles driven entirely by local shear and small-scale turbulence within the convective zone. Furthermore, we compared dynamo behaviors in both solar-type and anti-solar rotating scenarios, analyzing how rotation speed and the extent of differential rotation influence the resulting magnetic cycles.

Deep frameworks for multimodal learning have recently gained significant attention, yet existing research primarily focuses on two modes, limiting their applicability to scenarios involving more than two. This study introduces a generalized **K-fan multimodal deep framework** capable of handling data from *K* different sources. We represent each source through a **K-fan linear model**, where parameters are constrained by an $\ell_1$-norm regularizer to promote a sparse combination of features, ensuring each source relies on a limited subset of available data. Within the framework, we employ a deep neural network to model the nonlinear relationships between these sources and their joint latent representations. To handle the resulting non-convex optimization problem, we utilize the **alternating minimization approach**, while the intricate $\ell_1$-norm penalty involving multiple sources is resolved using the **generalized proximal gradient descent algorithm**. Experiments conducted on *K*-way classification tasks with multi-modal datasets demonstrate that the proposed method not only achieves superior classification accuracy but also offers a more interpretable representation of each data source compared to existing solutions.

Thread safety verification in multi-threaded programs remains a significant challenge. Model checking using Dynamic Partial Order Reduction (DPOR) has proven to be an effective technique for verifying this, yet current implementations are limited to basic operations like read/write and compare-and-swap. To address this, we introduce a general DPOR model checker that supports arbitrary operations defined by their pre- and post-conditions via simple programs. By leveraging the flexibility of this approach to validate complex thread-safe conditions, we anticipate more rigorous safety verification. Our prototype, McMini, was evaluated on 27 case studies from the literature, demonstrating that a condition expressed on 20 different operations could be verified in under one minute on a modern workstation.

The rapid dissemination of false information via social media has prompted researchers to explore effective mitigation strategies. WhatsApp, a dominant messaging platform widely used for personal communication, recently introduced a limit on message forwarding to address this issue. This study investigates whether enforcing such a restriction can successfully curb the spread of misinformation. Our findings indicate that message forwarding constitutes a secondary channel for disseminating false narratives rather than a primary one; consequently, even a complete ban on forwarding represents a modest impact. Furthermore, our data reveal that fewer than half of users adhere to the new forwarding limit. Ultimately, we conclude that current message controls within WhatsApp are insufficient to meaningfully reduce the overall propagation of false information.

This study examines a model of a large, supercritical branching population where mutations occur with low probability. We approximate the distribution of allelic frequencies by analyzing the distributions of type-specific ages within the surviving population. Furthermore, we derive the limiting age distribution for a specific class of supercritical branching processes with a Lebesgue-continuous density, noting its relationship to the age distribution observed in Crump-Mode-Jagers (CMJ) frameworks.

Deep learning techniques have proven highly effective across various speech recognition tasks, including the development of end-to-end (E2E) spoofing countermeasure systems. However, current state-of-the-art E2E architectures, such as those based on transformer models, still exhibit unsatisfactory performance. This study introduces a novel attention mechanism designed to enhance detection capabilities by refining how E2E systems attend to time-frequency features. Specifically, we propose an adaptive activation function for the query projections of cross-attention layers, aiming to mitigate information loss during feature encoding. Additionally, we developed two distinct weighted functions for the key and value projections of multi-head self-attention mechanisms; unlike standard linear weighting, these functions dynamically adjust the magnitude of transformer inputs based on specific time-frequency element characteristics. Experiments utilizing both standard and hybrid weighted functions demonstrate significant performance gains over the baseline.

We examine global supersymmetric effective field theories (EFTs) governing the inflaton, treating the slow-roll phase as Goldstone-like motion within the field space. Within this framework, the coefficients of the spatial gradients experienced by the Goldstone mode correspond to the coefficients of the holomorphic EFT functions $G$ and $\bar{G}$. Consequently, the non-standard kinetic terms influencing inflaton dynamics and their impact on fluctuations are restricted by the requirement that the kinetic matrix remains Hermitian. Furthermore, we investigate how these constraints on the matrix structure of the kinetic terms influence the statistical properties of primordial fluctuations.

Photon entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum information science, is typically characterized by symmetric correlation patterns between outputs from single-photon sources. In this work, we introduce and demonstrate the concept of asymmetric entanglement, defined as photon pair correlations that are not limited to integer counts of photons. Our experimental validation utilizes a standard type-II spontaneous parametric down-conversion setup, revealing a correlation where, on average, one output port emits two photons while the other emits none. This observation is corroborated by the violation of classical constraints imposed by a Bell inequality adapted for multi-photon states. Our findings not only introduce new perspectives on entanglement but also establish a resource with potential utility in information processing tasks.

Superconducting quantum circuits are a primary focus of current quantum information research. However, characterizing their electromagnetic modes is often difficult due to numerical and experimental uncertainties. This study utilizes Terahertz Scanning Near-field Optical Microscopy (SNOM) to investigate a planar microwave superconducting quantum electrodynamics (QED) setup. The research demonstrates that the THz SNFR technique can accurately capture electric fields within nanometer resolution, even when the scan probe is positioned near the surface. By correlating the measured data with finite element simulations, a clear field distribution corresponding to a specific cavity mode is established. Consequently, the method offers a novel means of experimentally verifying mode structures with high spatial precision, thereby aiding in the precise characterization of superconductive quantum apparatus.

Consider a finite collection of pairwise disjoint Borel sets $\{B_i\}_{i=1}^n$ that together cover the real axis. We address the inquiry of whether there exists a Bore set function $b: \mathcal{B} \to \mathbb{R}$ defined on the real axis such that for every $i$, the measure of $B_i$ is non-zero ($b(B_i) \neq 0$).

This work examines the potential impact of introducing new trading strategies on the performance of established market tactics. We employ an agent-based model featuring diverse investor types, each utilizing a specific strategy to determine trade actions. Initially, we validate the model's ability to replicate historical stock market characteristics, including the seasonality effect, before assessing the behavior of individual agents. Subsequently, we introduce a new trading rule to evaluate whether it generates profit without diminishing the returns of concurrent existing strategies. Our findings indicate that mixing strategy executions can degrade the profitability of established methods, suggesting that novel investment tactics may inadvertently reduce the alpha of current trading rules.

Current protocol detection techniques generally outperform manual inspections by offering superior transparency and security; however, their efficacy is undermined by the scarcity of rigorous testing against intentional attacks. This paper introduces a novel suite of malicious payloads designed to probe the standard TCP-based protocols—specifically Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP), Zebra Routing Protocol Daemon (Zebra/Zebra), and Zebra—used in network administration and detection. These payloads target specific message structures within the TCP layer to trigger unexpected behaviors in the Application layer, such as malformed frames, resulting in crashes, denial of service (DoS), or the exposure of sensitive system details. The provided proof of concept demonstrates the implementation and initial results of these attacks on popular open-source Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) and Security Monitoring Tools (SMTs), including Suricata, Snort, Zeek, and P0C. Furthermore, the paper presents a comprehensive framework and detailed methodology for evaluating the resilience of IDS and SMT solutions to such attacks, with extensive results and analysis on Suricata and Zeek included.

Placing a normal metal containing conduction electrons and a s-wave superconductor side-by-side induces the superconducting state into the metal through Andreev reflection. In this regime, Cooper pairs moving within the superconductor can coherently scatter backward into the metal, generating an effective, time-dependent pair density. Similarly, when this arrangement exists near a thin layer of magnet, the dynamically fluctuating spins of that metal can interact with the Cooper pairs to generate long-range magnon correlations across the superconductor. Consequently, effective magnon gates can be achieved by controlling either the superconducting order parameter or the movement of the Cooper pairs. Practical realizations of these mechanisms include using a magnetically biased spin spiral in a superconducting proximity layer to modulate magnon transmission, or adjusting an island's kinetic inductance via a Josephson junction to influence magnons connected to an adjacent superconducting plane.

Federated Learning (FL) offers a secure approach to distributed machine learning by distributing local training across devices, yet it faces significant challenges when handling new data classes that appear on some nodes but not others. This issue, known as Not-All-Equal-All-Classes (NAAAC) or, in this context, Novel Class Discovery within FL, can severely hinder model performance by causing negative transfer during class aggregation. To address this, the paper proposes Zero-Shot FL, a method that enables devices to locally classify previously unseen audio classes through class-level embeddings shared with a central server. On the other hand, devices encountering only standard classes contribute to a global model using standard loss functions. The authors evaluate their approach using the BENCHMARK dataset, which covers eight established sound categories and four novel ones introduced per federated participant. Empirical results indicate that Zero-Shot FL outperforms existing techniques, delivering superior accuracy on well-known categories while maintaining non-zero performance regarding newly introduced classes.

This manuscript outlines a strategy for the full multi-dimensional entanglement measurement (mFER) of multiqubit systems. Our proposed mFER enables the simultaneous acquisition of all joint observable outcomes for the entire hitherto unmeasured GHZ state cluster within a single trial. Leveraging quantum machine learning (QML), our comprehensive approach encompasses the simultaneous determination of every component of the full-order multiqubit coherence vector (CV). This method is designed to overcome the constraints of conventional full-state tomography (FST) and full-multi-parameter estimation (FMPE). Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces (IRS) are a key innovation in reconfiguring wireless networks, offering energy-efficient and low-cost enhancements to communication links. However, integrating IRS into multiuser environments introduces significant challenges, primarily due to the massive count of cascaded hardware components that necessitate channel estimation. To address this inefficiency, we propose a cascaded estimation method that eliminates the need for pilot signals regarding reconfigurable elements. Furthermore, a low-complexity joint design framework for optimizing phase shifts and allocating users is introduced. Simulation outcomes confirm that the suggested cascaded estimation strategy yields superior performance compared to conventional methods, while the proposed joint design achieves near-optimal results with substantially lower complexity.

This research investigates how local U.S. news online coverage shifted during the initial COVID-19 pandemic and examines the relationships between audience engagement and outcomes regarding cases, deaths, and preparedness. Coverage volume was measured by local news frequency on COVID-188 online stories from 2028 to March 2028. Audience involvement was assessed using two metrics: total page views per local news outlet and whether readers clicked on information regarding testing, vaccines, and mitigation strategies. Results indicate that local outlets concentrated their reporting heavily on the virus's economic impacts rather than on cases, deaths, or prevention methods. Furthermore, higher audience exposure to these coverage narratives was linked to greater anxiety and reduced confidence in local government handling of the crisis.

Counting represents a fundamental early-acquired skill in children, yet its developmental timeline remains unclear. To investigate this, we present a novel computational model that replicates this acquisition process. The system leverages Recurrent Units equipped with Memory Augmentation to retain prior interactions and sustain internal state over time. By pre-training these networks via a self-supervised task involving next-token prediction on a dataset of natural language descriptions, the model successfully acquires the ability to count post-fine-tuning, demonstrating a superior capacity compared to standard RNNs or Transformers to do so. Furthermore, visualizing the learned latent manifolds reveals structured organization aligned with numerical magnitude, offering fresh insights into how counting ability emerges.

The bloom filter, a space-efficient probabilistic data structure for rapid set membership verification, has seen significant developments, most notably the Cuckoo filter. This paper introduces a new filter design, inspired by the Xor matrix used in approximate counting, which offers both reduced memory usage and faster filter operations compared to the Cuckoo filter.

This study examines the market directional data generated by the sequence of transaction events, where each event specifies a time stamp, execution price, and volume traded. The approach utilizes a pricing and hedging framework grounded in a general framework of transaction flow that encompasses both intra-market trading and future market interactions. It is demonstrated that, provided transaction future impacts are not excessively severe, there exists a equivalent representation where futures trading is prohibited; in this alternative model, transaction costs alone govern the direction and structure of future market activity.

Current distributed machine learning frameworks prioritize data privacy by retaining datasets locally across devices while transmitting only model parameters to an aggregator. However, because these parameters encode traces of the training data, their transmission exposes the system to rogue device attacks that can corrupt the global model. While some existing solutions attempt to mitigate such attacks, they often fail to balance robustness and communication efficiency adequately. In response, we introduce FLVoogd, a streamlined and efficient aggregation framework designed to defend against arbitrary malicious inputs from compromised devices. This protocol achieves a remarkable 98% immunity to attacks with only a minor increase in communication overhead, making it applicable across various model architectures. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that FLVoogd surpasses existing methods in both robustness and efficiency. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/voogd/FLVoogd.

While recent advancements in deep learning have transformed robotics, a persistent challenge remains the disparity between artificial simulation and real-world deployment. Robots often excel in synthetic environments but struggle when faced with actual reality. To counter this, researchers have introduced "sim2real" bridging techniques that narrow the gap between simulation and life. This paper introduces a new Sim2Real bridging approach grounded in gradient-based domain adaptation. The method utilizes one-way translation through an autoencoder to first learn shared features across domains and then maps images specifically from simulation to reality. We applied this framework to the task of driving simulation to reality, employing an incremental training methodology that begins pre-training on synthetic data before fine-tuning on real-world images. To evaluate this approach, we conducted extensive experiments on the nuScenes dataset alongside various baseline models. The results demonstrate a significant reduction in the domain gap, with our method outperforming all baseline comparisons.

Deepfake technology employs deep learning to create or modify media content, resulting in widespread adoption across numerous industries. Although the field has advanced significantly over the last few years, current research remains largely confined to specific, limited datasets. This study introduces a comprehensive framework for generating and detecting deepfakes across unrestricted audio and video content. The proposed detection system utilizes an ensemble of multiple classifiers that analyze various cues within the media to identify manipulation traces. Empirical results demonstrate a substantial improvement in accuracy compared to existing methods. Additionally, the researchers developed an automated quality metric for deepfake detection that shows a strong positive correlation with human perception of anomalies.

This work presents a foundational study on the sequential processing capabilities of simple biologically realistic spiking neural networks. We introduce a new learning framework designed to extract discrete symbolic sequences and demonstrate that an unsupervised, self-organizing mechanism can acquire sequential knowledge in these networks. The proposed method relies on two key mechanisms: first, an unsupervised self-organization process that partitions spiking activity into distinct groups, and second, an unsupervised, self-adjusting rule that progressively lengthens the temporal window of memory. We further show through both an artificial made-up sequence and human language data that these networks can unsupervisedly master sequential patterns. Finally, a direct comparison with human forgetting curves reveals a comparable decay rate in memory retention among the simulated networks and actual biological systems.

This paper introduces the "Out-of-Category" challenge, a framework designed to evaluate the adaptability of zero-shot image classification systems when confronted with novel categories. To achieve this assessment, we present the Out-of-Category Challenge Report, detailing the experimental setup, submitted results, and author insights. The experiments were conducted using the ImageNet dataset, which was partitioned into three mutually exclusive sets: source, target, and challenge. The aim is to train models exclusively on source categories and test their performance on target categories, with a specific focus on generalizing to the challenge subset which contains unseen classes. This rigorous testing protocol seeks to verify whether truly generalized zero-shot models can accurately classify entirely new categories. The paper concludes by offering a comprehensive analysis of the outcomes and identifying potential future research avenues.

This study presents an efficient approach for dynamically verifying A posteriori stochastic models that utilize generalized polynomial chaos (GPC) expansions. The core technique involves comparing solutions derived from truncated GPC representations against those from direct deterministic integration against specific test functions. The difference between these solutions serves as an error indicator to assess both the accuracy of direct numerical integration and GPC expansion coefficients. By leveraging an interpolating quadrature rule for the comparison step, the method minimizes integration errors, allowing variations in residual GPC coefficients alone to act as a reliable metric for total model error. If these residual variations exceed a predefined tolerance, the indicators signal potential issues with either direct integration accuracy or GPC coefficient determination, prompting refinements such as increasing polynomial degrees or enhancing direct integration precision until solution reliability is confirmed.

This paper introduces a new approach to adaptive sequential change detection that addresses a critical limitation in current methods: their inability to handle uncertainties regarding the specific causal source of a change. While existing techniques can identify that a change has occurred, they often fail to distinguish whether the root cause lies in a specific subsystem or in an external, environmental factor. By equipping agents with the capability to detect changes in both system components and the surroundings, our solution enables more precise, cost-effective responses tailored to the nature of the issue rather than applying a uniform strategy. The proposed methodology is formalized as a problem of sequentially identifying and isolating changes under partially observability conditions, grounded in a multi-agent framework involving a specific agent, multiple system subsystems, and the external environment. The core algorithm relies on a computationally efficient mechanism for estimating the agent's belief state, utilizing a sequential proportionally adjusted filter to track the probability of interaction with system subsystems and a separate sequential binary change detector for the environment. Simulation results involving unknown shifts in agent dynamics, system behaviors, and environmental conditions demonstrate that this approach achieves performance comparable to optimal Bayesian estimates while maintaining significantly lower computational costs.

Unlike traditional approaches, this technique does not require assumptions regarding the initial mass function (IMF) or specific nucleosynthetic yields, and it is capable of capturing temporal variations in the IMF and yields over cosmic time. Extracting structured data from visual documents is a difficult yet vital task with broad applications. While state-of-the-art models have largely shifted toward vision-centric architectures, assembling high-quality training datasets remains both labor-intensive and expensive, especially as models now handle multiple visual modalities requiring diverse annotation tools and expert personnel. To address this, we introduce a zero-shot semi-supervised transfer learning strategy that utilizes unlabeled data to expand upon initial labeled sets. We demonstrate that augmenting a base dataset of just 100 items with 10,000 unlabeled samples via fine-tuning boosts extraction performance by 10% to 20% compared to standard baselines. Furthermore, our method offers significant cost reductions by enabling the training of high-performing systems on specific layouts with only a handful of sample annotations.

Indium antimonide (InAs) serves as a leading candidate for host materials in topological insulator systems due to its highly efficient mercury quantum well formation capabilities. In this study, we investigate the electronic structure at EuS/InAs interfaces using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES). Our findings reveal that the interfaces exhibit distinct electronic structures that vary depending on whether the samples are prepared with "top-down" or "bottom-up" configurations. Specifically, "top-down" samples display Fermi surface states resembling those of bulk EuS, whereas "bottom-up" samples exhibit novel interface-specific electronic states not present in bulk EuS. These observations indicate that the quality of the EuS/InAs interface critically influences the resulting electronic structure.

This paper presents an efficient method for representing each Borel class in the Wadge hierarchy, leading to an improved classification of such classes that resolves the classification problem first raised by Lachlan and Sasso. Our approach achieves this by establishing a bi-reduction between Borewale Wadge classes and pairs consisting of Borewale languages and $\Sigma^0_1$ (i.e., recursively enumerable) partial functions.

The merger of neutron stars and neutron star–black hole systems generates gravitational waves that share a universal waveform structure, distinguishable only by a few key parameters: the total mass, mass ratio, effective spin, and effective chirp mass. This study demonstrates that these quantities can be precisely extracted from waveform data using deep learning models. We trained a classification algorithm on numerical relativity simulations of NS-NS and NS-BH mergers, covering a broad spectrum of mass ratios, effective spins, and chirp masses. The model achieved high accuracy in merger classification and in estimating the total mass and mass ratio. Additionally, we developed a dedicated regressor for the effective spin, which performed well even when applied to data outside the specific mass range used for training. These findings suggest that the data-driven approach is robust and reliable for analyzing gravitational waveforms from NS-NS and NS-BH mergers.

We report the discovery of an exoplanet, TOI-5542 b, identified via a combination of TESS photometry, high-precision radial velocity data from HARPS and CARMENES, and follow-up observations using HARPS-N, APIS, and NIRSPEC. This system is notable for being the first discovered outside the Sun's galactic neighborhood, as it orbits a metal-poor G-dwarf located approximately 1,000 parsecs away. The planet exhibits a 3.36-day orbital period with a minimum mass of 0.61 $M_{\rm J}$ and an inclination of $89.9^\circ$, suggesting a near-circular orbit ($e=0.002$) at a semi-major axis of 0.055 au. Based on an estimated equilibrium temperature of 1500 K, the host star's age of roughly 8.2 billion years, and the planet's short period, it is likely a highly evolved gas giant. We also present the initial characterization of this ancient, metal-deficient host star.

We address a constrained Markov decision process (CMDP) involving a finite state and action space alongside $K$ constraints. By reformulating the problem as a zero-sum game between two agents, we propose a Primal-Dual Method (PDM) rooted in the Min-Max Theorem. This iterative approach alternates between updating dual variables and performing the optimal policy for the corresponding primal subproblem. We establish the convergence of this iteration toward a saddle point of the zero-sum game, thereby yielding an $\epsilon$-approximate solution to the original CMDC. Furthermore, we derive a complexity bound for the PDM, demonstrating its superiority over prior methods specifically when dealing with a large number of dual variables.

This paper outlines a methodology for detecting handwritten mathematical notation through the integration of two deep learning models: a recurrent neural network (LSTM) to classify symbols and a convolutional neural network (CNN) to locate them. This approach addresses the limitations of prior research, which relied on CNNs for recognition and often struggled with overlapping characters or misaligned bounding boxes. By employing an NN-based segmentation step, our system achieves precise identification regardless of character density, while the notation parsing phase extracts structured data to support syntactic analysis.

We investigate a novel application of superconformal supersymmetry within the quantum mechanics of a particle moving in a sheaf-cohomology-driven, inhomogeneous, and electrically anisotropic periodic landscape. Our analysis reveals that this system's supersymmetry is exclusively preserved in the sheaf-cohomology fundamental period, whereas it breaks in higher-order cohorts. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the eigenvalue $| \lambda |$ associated with the supercharges' fermionic parity operator $\lambda$ functions as a precise regulator for the sheaf cohomology's exponential growth as the quantum scale expands.

Interactions among agents within complex networks serve as a fundamental mechanism for information and resource exchange in both social ecosystems and biological systems. While existing research predominantly addresses equilibrium states, this study investigates the dynamic variability of interaction processes throughout their temporal evolution. By analyzing the standard deviation of actual versus expected return times to node encounters, we reveal a universal behavior characterized by a power law distribution. Furthermore, this study examines how mean and power-law exponents of these distribution profiles are influenced by network topology, specifically through the degree heterogeneity and clustering.

Recent investigations have demonstrated that the parameter updates employed by the policy network in actor-critic reinforcement learning (RL) align with the stochastic gradient Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) moves of the maximization component of the mean-field variational lower bound for the actor-critic framework. This correspondence reveals that the policy network's role in this update mechanism functions as the Hamiltonian system's perturbation term. Building on this insight, we introduce a novel enhanced actor-critic model that explicitly leverages the Hamiltonian Monte Carlo component from the update rules. Experimental results across multiple testbeds indicate that this new algorithm significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods, delivering superior sample efficiency.

In this paper, the twin prime conjecture is proven by establishing that there are infinitely many pairs of primes $p$ and $p+2$. The proof proceeds by contradiction: if there were only finitely many such pairs, say $p_1 < p_2 < \dots < p_n$, the arguments demonstrate this scenario leads to a logical impossibility.

This research introduces a real-time Sonar integration module designed to bolster the layered navigation controller. It aggregates data from multiple sonar sensors, each covering a 30-degree field of view, to deliver a 360-degree environment perception. By merging this spatial awareness with layered navigation controller principles, the system achieves enhanced obstacle avoidance capabilities. The proposed system has been implemented in MATLAB, with its performance evaluated through simulation.

Dwarf planets Nereid and Triton are recognized as the coldest and most distant bodies in the Solar System with well-documented surfaces dominated by nitrogen ice and water ice. While the 2015 New Horizons flyby of Pluto revealed complex water ice textures, the surface composition of Nereid remains poorly understood. This study utilizes NIR reflectance data from the Hubble Space Telescope to constrain the water ice content in Nereid's ice mixtures. We modeled these mixtures using a linear combination of water ice spectra and nitrogen ice spectra, derived from the New Horizons Ralph/Visible and Pluto/MRCS instruments respectively. Our analysis indicates that a 50/50 nitrogen/water ice mixture is inconsistent with the observed reflectance, as it would produce a water ice band depth approximately 20% greater than what was measured. Conversely, a mixture rich in nitrogen ice (Nixie ice) aligns closely with the data, allowing for up to 10% water ice by volume. These findings suggest that water ice on Nereid is significantly scarcer than on Pluto's surface, which contains up to 30% water ice.

Dynamic treatment regimes are sequential decision-making frameworks designed to determine optimal treatment plans for individuals, with a specific focus on those exhibiting complex, multi-factor health issues. These regimes are particularly valuable in medical contexts where patient outcomes hinge on a combination of baseline characteristics and prior treatment history. The primary objective of this work is to investigate a Bayesian learning method for constructing these regimes, aiming to maximize the net positivity of a net benefit function. This function accounts for both net clinical value and clinical complexity. By integrating utility gains against the costs associated with treatment complexity, the resulting Bayesian policy offers a balanced approach to patient care. The study also addresses the computationally demanding nature of the resulting high-dimensional, structured Markov decision problem. To resolve this, we develop a specialized simulation annealing algorithm, enhancing its performance by introducing a tailored metropolis criterion and an optimized proposal distribution specific to the medical domain. Furthermore, we present a new Bayesian methodology for estimating the parameters of our core model. Validation through a comprehensive simulation framework, utilizing real-world data from the Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort (CRIC) trial, demonstrates that the proposed approach is both effective and feasible.
